docs.title: Cobblemon PokeGyms
docs.text:
Not released yet

PokeGyms has no public download yet. These pages describe the current development build, 0.0.47. What it does today is find the gyms, give each City gym an RCT leader you can fight, after its RCT disciples of the leader's type, let you challenge the leader of a player-held gym (a loser pays its penalty into the gym's vault, a winner gets a signed medal, a Badge It badge if the gym has one, and a challenger waits before a rematch), scale every RCT trainer's team, leaders included, to your level (stage and moves too), let a leader invite up to three disciples who you fight in order before the leader, let the leader share the vault with them, let a player take a held gym over with its leader's medal, let a challenger call out the gym's next trainer from the Gym Manager, let a leader write what the gym's NPC says during a challenge, stage each leader battle at the gym's own spots, count the gym fights Cobblemon Action Combat runs in real time, stand a Champion behind a lectern for whoever carries eight badges, ban Tera, Dynamax, Mega Evolution, Z-Moves and held items on the gym's side of a battle, run their Gym Manager and tell other mods which battles are gym battles.

docs.title: Cobblemon PokeGyms
docs.text:
Gyms for Cobblemon multiplayer servers. PokeGyms finds the gym building of every Kanto city that Cobblemon Cities & Structures generates, records it for the world, and stands a Gym Manager inside its door: the one place where everything about that gym happens.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+ Needs CobbleDollars + Radical Cobblemon Trainers + Cities & Structures

Get started The Gym Manager

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 🏙️ Every Cities & Structures gym, found: Pewter, Cerulean, Vermilion, Celadon, Fuchsia, Saffron, Cinnabar and Viridian, also in worlds generated before PokeGyms was installed.
  • 📖 A Gym Manager in every gym: a lectern just inside the door that opens the gym's own screen, titled by its city, such as "Pewter City Gym".
  • 🏛️ A Radical Cobblemon Trainers leader in every City gym: every gym starts as a City gym, led by one of RCT's own gym leaders.
  • 🥊 Fight the City leader: a stake of CobbleDollars, and it stays out of RCT's progression.
  • 🧑‍🎓 City disciples: up to three RCT trainers of the leader's type, fought weakest first before the leader.
  • 🔓 Beat the leader, unlock the gym: only a player who beats a City leader may buy that gym's licence.
  • 🎫 Licences: the rules for owning a gym are in place, one licence per player on the whole server.
  • 💰 The gym vault: a player leader sets a penalty, a challenger who loses pays it into the gym's vault, and the holder withdraws it.
  • 🏆 Winner's share: beat a player leader and you take a share of its vault, 10% by default.
  • 🧑‍🏫 Disciples: a player leader invites up to three players, who register a team and stand at the gym as Gym Trainer <player>; challengers beat them in order before the leader.
  • 🤝 Vault split: the leader gives each disciple a share of the vault, and a withdrawal pays everyone at once.
  • 🔁 Take a gym over: hold the medal you won from a player leader and pay the fee, and the gym is yours, vault and disciples included.
  • 🏅 Signed medals: beat a player leader and you get a Gym Medal that names the gym, the leader and the date, or a signed Badge It badge when the leader registered one.
  • 🎖️ Mainline badges: with PKGBadges installed, beating a City leader gives the badge that leader gives in the main games.
  • 📈 Level scaling: a leader's team, and every RCT trainer's, fights at the level of your best Pokémon, up or down, evolution stage included, so a battle is fair at any stage.
  • ⚔️ Gym battles, recognised: a battle against a trainer inside a gym counts as a gym battle, so other mods can reward it, such as Mid-Battle EXP's extra EXP in gyms.
  • ⚡ Real-time fights count: with Cobblemon Action Combat installed, a gym fight it runs in real time gives the same medal, vault share, badge, unlock or penalty as a turn-based one.
  • 👑 The Champion: craft a Champion's Lectern, carry eight badges from different gyms, beat a level 70 team and take the trophy home; lose and the penalty is destroyed.
  • 🚫 Battle rules: the server, and each leader for their own gym, can ban Tera, Dynamax, Mega Evolution, Z-Moves and held items on the gym's side; challengers battle as always.
  • ⚙️ Tuned in game with /pokegyms config, no restart needed.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Version 0.0.47 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8+ — 1.7.x is not supported Also needs CobbleDollars, Radical Cobblemon Trainers, Cobblemon Cities & Structures — Radical Cobblemon Trainers with its RCT API. Without Cities & Structures PokeGyms starts but finds no gyms Fabric Fabric Language Kotlin, Architectury API NeoForge Kotlin for Forge, Architectury API Optional Badge It: the leader registers one of its badges as the gym's medal · PKGBadges: beating a City leader gives that leader's mainline badge · Cobblemon Action Combat: its real-time gym fights give their result like a turn-based one

No public download yet. New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: The Champion
docs.text: Once you carry enough badges, the world has one more trainer to beat: its Champion, a Radical Cobblemon Trainers (RCT) trainer of RCT's own champion type. The Champion stands behind a Champion's Lectern. Beat it and you get a trophy; lose and you pay for it.

docs.title: The Champion's Lectern
docs.text:
The lectern is a block you craft and place, and it is the only way to get a Champion. It is in the creative tab too.

Shaped recipe (3 gold blocks, 1 diamond block, 1 lectern):

Gold block Diamond block Gold block Lectern Gold block
  • One Champion per world. The lectern you placed last is this world's; the Champion stands behind it, facing the side you read it from. Placing another retires the older lectern and its Champion goes. Clicking a retired lectern says so.
  • Breaking this world's lectern sends the Champion away, and there is none until a lectern is placed again. The lectern drops itself.
  • The Champion is picked once. It is one of RCT's champion trainers, the same one for the same world. Without a champion trainer in RCT there is no Champion, and the lectern says it is not ready.
  • Click the lectern, or the Champion, to challenge. Both do the same.

docs.title: Who may challenge
docs.text:
PokeGyms refuses the challenge and says why unless all of this holds:

  • Eight badges from different gyms. A badge is a signed medal (or Badge It badge) in your inventory, or a City gym whose leader you beat (or whose mainline badge you got). A gym counts once, however many medals you carry from it. Medals in a chest do not count: carry them.
  • The penalty in hand. You need at least the penalty (5000 CobbleDollars by default), because that is what losing costs.
  • No cooldown running. See Rematch.
  • Nobody else fighting the Champion. There is one Champion, so one fight at a time.
  • The Champion is open. An operator can close it.

docs.title: The battle
docs.text:
• Level 70 at least. The Champion's team is scaled to your best Pokémon like every RCT trainer's, but never under level 70, however low your party is. It never goes over the server's maximum level.
  • Outside RCT's progression, like a City leader: beating it does not advance your RCT trainer progress.
  • It is a gym battle for other mods, and counts with Cobblemon Action Combat when that mod runs the fight in real time.

docs.title: Rematch and the trophy
docs.text:
• Win: a trophy. The Champion's Trophy names the Champion you beat and the date you won it, in its tooltip. You get one per win, and it drops at your feet when your inventory is full.
  • Lose: the penalty is destroyed. Forfeiting or running away is a loss. The CobbleDollars are taken from you and paid to nobody. A fight the server stops with no winner costs nothing.
  • Either result starts a cooldown, the same rematch cooldown setting as the player leaders (rematch.cooldown_minutes, 60 minutes by default). It is yours alone, and survives a restart. With rematch switched off there is no wait.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
An operator tunes the Champion with /pokegyms config champion:

Setting Default What it does champion.enabled true Off: the Champion takes no challenges. Trophies already won stay, and a battle already running finishes, a loss still costing the penalty. champion.badges 8 Medals and badges from different gyms a challenger must carry. champion.level_floor 70 The lowest level the Champion's team fights at. 1 lets it scale freely. champion.penalty 5000 What losing costs, in CobbleDollars, and the least a challenger must have to start.

docs.title: Commands & Configuration
docs.text: Every command is under /pokegyms, for operators only (permission level 2).

docs.title: /pokegyms gyms
docs.text:
Lists every gym the server has found in your current dimension, one line each: its coordinates, its status (canonical, vacant, or held by a player), the city structure it stands in, and how many of its eight marks PokeGyms read (8/8 markers is a gym with every mark; a gym recorded before 0.0.43 shows 5/8, and works, it only has no battle staging).

Click the coordinates to get a /tp to that gym's Gym Manager in your chat box.

docs.title: /pokegyms battles
docs.text: Lists the gym battles running now, one line each: the battle's id, who the challenger faces (leader, disciple or canonical_leader), and the gym's coordinates and dimension, as /pokegyms gyms lists them. With none running, it says No gym battles running.

docs.title: /pokegyms config
docs.text:
Shows and changes every setting on a live server. A change takes effect at once, without a restart, and is written to the config file so it survives one.

Command What it does /pokegyms config Lists every feature with its settings. /pokegyms config licences Lists one feature. A value that is not the default shows the default beside it. /pokegyms config licences enabled <true\|false> Switches the whole feature on or off. /pokegyms config licences <setting> <value> Sets a number, within the setting's range. /pokegyms config canonical penalty <value> The same for the City-leader battle; canonical takes enabled and reset like licences. /pokegyms config leader enabled <true\|false> Opens or closes team registration; leader has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config vault <setting> <value> Sets penalty_min or penalty_max of the gym vault; vault takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config winner_share <setting> <value> Sets percent of the winner's share of the vault; winner_share takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config rematch <setting> <value> Sets cooldown_minutes of the rematch cooldown; rematch takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config scaling enabled <true\|false> Switches level scaling, of gym leaders and RCT trainers, on or off; scaling has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config evolution enabled <true\|false> Switches the evolution stage of scaled teams on or off; needs scaling on, evolution has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config medals enabled <true\|false> Switches the medal for beating a player leader on or off; medals has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config badges enabled <true\|false> Switches the mainline badge for beating a City leader on or off; badges has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config disciples enabled <true\|false> Switches disciples on or off; disciples has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config city_disciples enabled <true\|false> Switches the City disciples on or off; city_disciples has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config takeover <setting> <value> Sets fee of a gym takeover; takeover takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config vault_split enabled <true\|false> Switches the vault split among leader and disciples on or off; vault_split has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config roster enabled <true\|false> Switches the Roster tab for challengers on or off; roster has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config dialogue <setting> <value> Sets max_length of a leader's line; dialogue takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config staging <setting> <value> Sets doubles_gap of battle staging; staging takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config champion <setting> <value> Sets badges, level_floor or penalty of the Champion; champion takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config rules <setting> <0\|1> Sets allow_tera, allow_dynamax, allow_mega, allow_z or allow_held_items of the battle rules: 0 bans, 1 allows; rules takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config licences reset Puts the feature back to its defaults, switched on.

Licences already held stay, and still expire or can be renounced. licences.price 25000 0 or more What a gym's licence costs, in CobbleDollars. licences.expiry_days 30 0 to 36,500 Days a holder can stay offline before their licence ends. 0 keeps a licence for good. canonical.enabled true Off: City gym leaders take no challenges. Vaults keep their money, can still be withdrawn, and are still paid out when a licence ends. vault.penalty_min 100 0 or more The least a holder may set as their gym's penalty, in CobbleDollars. Battles already running keep theirs. evolution.enabled true Off: a scaled team keeps its registered species instead of taking the evolution stage of its new level. Needs scaling on. medals.enabled true Off: beating a player leader gives no medal. Medals already given stay. badges.enabled true Off: beating a City leader gives no badge. Badges already given stay. winner_share.enabled true Off: beating a player leader takes nothing from the vault. winner_share.percent 10 0 to 100 The share of the gym's vault the winner takes, rounded down. 0 takes nothing. disciples.enabled true Off: a holder cannot invite, and an invited player cannot accept or register. Disciples already there stay, and the holder can still remove them. city_disciples.enabled true Off: City gyms put no RCT disciples out and their leader is challenged directly. The ones already chosen stay saved and stand again when it is back on. takeover.enabled true Off: nobody can take a held gym over. Gyms already taken stay as they are. takeover.fee 10000 0 or more What taking a gym over costs, in CobbleDollars. It is destroyed, never paid to anyone. vault_split.enabled true Off: the whole vault goes to the leader and no share can be set. The shares already set are kept for when it is back on. roster.enabled true Off: challengers get no Roster tab. Clicking a trainer still challenges it, in the same order. dialogue.enabled true Off: gym leaders and disciples say nothing and the battle starts at once. Saved lines are kept. dialogue.max_length 120 1 to 256 The longest a leader's line may be, in characters. A longer line is refused and nothing is saved. staging.enabled true Off: leader battles are not staged: nobody is moved and Cobblemon places every Pokémon. staging.doubles_gap 3 1 to 8 Blocks between the two Pokémon of one side in a staged doubles battle. champion.enabled true Off: the Champion takes no challenges. Trophies already won stay, and a battle already running finishes, a loss still costing the penalty. champion.badges 8 1 to 64 Medals and badges from different gyms a challenger must carry to challenge the Champion. champion.level_floor 70 1 to 1,000 The lowest level the Champion's team fights at, however low the challenger's party. 1 lets it scale freely. champion.penalty 5000 0 or more What losing to the Champion costs, in CobbleDollars, and the least a challenger must carry to start. It is destroyed, never paid to anyone. rules.enabled true Off: gym battles allow every gimmick and held item, whatever the allow_* settings and the leaders' own bans say. The bans stay saved and count again when it is back on. rules.allow_tera true false bans Terastallization on the gym's side of every gym battle. rules.allow_dynamax true false bans Dynamax. rules.allow_mega true false bans Mega Evolution. rules.allow_z true false bans Z-Moves, and Ultra Burst with them. rules.allow_held_items true false takes every held item off the gym's battling Pokémon.

A setting missing from the file takes its default, and one out of range is pulled into it; the file is then written back whole, so you always find every setting in it. A file that is not valid JSON is left as it is, and the server runs on the defaults and says so in its log.

See Licences for what a licence does.

docs.title: Community Credits
docs.text:
PokeGyms is built on the work of others:

  • Cobblemon, whose summary screen the Gym Manager is built on.
  • Cobblemon Cities & Structures, whose Kanto cities, gym buildings and leaders PokeGyms runs.
  • CobbleDollars, the currency gym licences are paid in.
  • Radical Cobblemon Trainers, whose trainers and API PokeGyms builds on.

Found a bug or have an idea? Post it in the Discord.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: PokeGyms targets Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge, with Cobblemon 1.8. It is made for multiplayer servers, and it goes on the server and on every player's game.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Notes Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader 0.18.0+ or NeoForge the jar for your loader Fabric Language Kotlin or Kotlin for Forge the one for your loader Architectury API both loaders Cobblemon 1.8.0+ 1.7.x is not supported CobbleDollars 2.0.0+ the currency licences are paid in Radical Cobblemon Trainers 0.19.2-beta+ with its RCT API 0.16.2-beta+ Cobblemon Cities & Structures the cities whose gyms PokeGyms runs

Optional: Badge It, so a gym's medal can be one of its badges (Medals), and PKGBadges, so beating a City leader gives that leader's mainline badge (Mainline badges).

PokeGyms starts without Cities & Structures, but then it finds no gyms and does nothing. With an older version of any of the others, the game refuses to start and names the mod and the version it needs.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Cobblemon, CobbleDollars, Radical Cobblemon Trainers with RCT API, Cobblemon Cities & Structures and the libraries for your loader.
  2. Drop the PokeGyms jar for your loader into mods/, on the server and on every player's game. Never put both loaders' jars in.
  3. Start the server. Existing worlds work: a city generated before PokeGyms was installed has its gym found the first time it loads.
  4. Walk into the gym of a Cities & Structures Kanto city. The Gym Manager lectern stands just inside the door; right-click it.

An operator can list every gym the server has found in the current dimension with /pokegyms gyms (Commands).

docs.title: Which gyms
docs.text:
PokeGyms runs the gym buildings of Cobblemon Cities & Structures. Eight of its Kanto cities can have one:

Pewter · Cerulean · Vermilion · Celadon · Fuchsia · Saffron · Cinnabar · Viridian

Lavender and Pallet have no gym, and a city does not always build its gym, so not every city you find has one. That is Cities & Structures' choice; PokeGyms records the gyms that are there.

A gym is found the first time its city loads, new or generated long before PokeGyms was installed, and it is remembered for that world from then on, across restarts. Each dimension keeps its own list.

docs.title: City gyms and their leaders
docs.text:
Every gym starts as a City gym, led by one of Radical Cobblemon Trainers' own gym leaders (the leader_* trainers, 24 different names in RCT 0.19.2).

  • One leader per City, kept for good. PokeGyms picks the leader the first time the gym is found and remembers it. No leader's name repeats across the world's gyms until every one has been used.
  • The leader stands still and cannot be hurt, at the gym's leader spot. The Gym Manager names them.
  • Cities & Structures' own leader is removed. PokeGyms puts RCT's leader in their place, so the gym never has two. Worlds made before this version change over by themselves the next time each gym loads.
  • A gym that is no longer a City gym loses its RCT leader.

docs.title: City disciples
docs.text:
While a City gym is still its own leader's, up to three Radical Cobblemon Trainers stand at its disciple spots, like the disciples of a player gym.

  • They share the leader's type: the type found most often among the primary and secondary types of the leader's team. A tie goes to the type of the leader's last Pokémon.
  • They are ordinary RCT trainers: never a gym leader, Elite Four member, champion, rival or villain boss. The City chooses them once, so a gym always has the same ones. A type with fewer than three such trainers gives the ones there are.
  • Fought weakest to strongest, by the highest level in each one's team.
  • Beat them all before the leader. The leader takes a challenge only once you have beaten every one. Each fight needs the penalty in hand. Winning costs nothing; losing to one takes the penalty (destroyed, as against the leader) and sends you back to the first. A finished leader challenge starts the next one from the first again, and your progress survives logouts and restarts.
  • They step aside while a player holds the gym, which has its own disciples, and stand again when the City leader returns.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config city_disciples enabled false: no City disciples stand and the City leader is challenged directly.

docs.title: Fighting a City leader
docs.text:
Right-click the leader to challenge them, once you have beaten the leader's disciples. PokeGyms starts the battle with the leader's RCT team, but it does not count in RCT's progression: winning does not raise your level cap or add the leader to your defeat list, and RCT gives no loot or dialogue for it.

  • You need CobbleDollars to start. You must carry at least the penalty, canonical.penalty (1,000 by default). If you are short, you are told how much you need.
  • Losing costs the penalty. Losing, forfeiting or running away takes exactly that sum from you. The money goes to no one. Winning costs nothing, and unlocks the gym's licence for you.
  • One challenger at a time per leader. A second challenger is told the leader is busy.
  • A win can also give a badge. See Mainline badges.
  • Operators can close the fight or change the penalty with /pokegyms config canonical. Closed, leaders take no challenges; battles already running finish, and a loss still costs the penalty.

docs.title: Unlocking a City gym
docs.text:
A City gym's licence is not for sale to everyone: only a player who beats its leader in the fight above may buy it (see Licences).

  • A win unlocks it for the winner only. You are told in chat, the Info tab says you may buy the licence, and the Licence tab appears. Everyone else who opens the Gym Manager is told to beat the leader first, and the server refuses their purchase.
  • Nothing else counts. Losing, running away, a battle that is stopped, or beating the leader outside PokeGyms' own fight unlocks nothing.
  • The leader steps aside while the gym is held. When the winner buys the licence, the RCT leader leaves the gym and takes no challenge.
  • When the licence ends, the leader returns. Renouncing or expiring puts the leader back and locks the gym again for everyone, the former holder included: they must beat the leader anew.
  • Your win is remembered even if licences are switched off, so it still counts when they are switched back on.

docs.title: Registering your team
docs.text:
A gym's holder (the player who holds its licence, in a town gym or in a City gym won from its leader) can register their party as the gym's team. The gym then has a leader of its own.

  • Open the Team tab of the Gym Manager, pick singles or doubles, and press Register. Singles takes 1 Pokémon from your party, doubles takes 2. Only the holder sees the tab, and the server checks it again when you press the button.
  • The gym keeps a frozen copy. The Pokémon are copied, healed, and the copy does not follow yours: you keep your own Pokémon and can train, trade or lose them. Registering again replaces the copy.
  • Everyone sees the team. The gym team panel on the Gym Manager's side lists the registered Pokémon by name and level.
  • A leader NPC stands for it. Gym Leader <player> stands at the gym's leader spot, wearing the holder's skin (default or slim, read from their Minecraft profile) and carrying the copy as its party. It cannot be hurt, moved or pushed, and does not despawn. If it is killed, it comes back the next time its chunk loads.
  • It leaves when the licence ends. Renouncing or expiring removes the team, the NPC and the gym's disciples. In a City gym, the RCT leader returns at the same time (see Unlocking a City gym). An NPC whose chunk was unloaded when the licence ended is removed the next time that chunk loads.
  • Operators can close registration with /pokegyms config leader. Off, nobody can register or replace a team; teams already registered stay, with their leader.

Worlds saved before this version load every gym with no team. A saved team that cannot be read is dropped and the gym is kept.

docs.title: Challenging a gym
docs.text:
Right-click the Gym Leader NPC of a player-held gym to fight the team its holder registered.

  • The holder picks the format. It is singles or doubles, whatever the holder registered.
  • Who cannot challenge. The holder cannot challenge their own gym. A gym with no holder or no registered team takes no challenge, and neither does a leader who is already battling someone else (you are told it is busy).
  • You need the penalty in hand. The holder sets a penalty for their gym, and you must carry at least that many CobbleDollars to challenge. A loss moves exactly the penalty into the gym's vault; a win or a stopped battle costs nothing, and a win takes a share of that vault. If you are short, you are told how much it costs and what you have.
  • The result counts once. Winning or losing tells you in chat. Forfeiting or running away counts as a loss. A battle the server stops counts as nothing.
  • The leader always fields a fresh copy of the team. Used PP or berries from an earlier battle do not carry over, and the gym's registered team is never changed.
  • Nobody's Pokémon are hurt. The battle uses a copy of your party, so your Pokémon keep their health, and it gives no XP or EVs for the same reason.
  • In a City gym held by a player, the fight counts as against the player leader, not the City leader: it does not touch the City leader's unlock or penalty, and /pokegyms battles lists it as leader.
  • A rematch has to wait. See Rematch cooldown.
  • The penalty has its own switch. /pokegyms config vault turns it off: nobody pays or needs one to challenge.
  • It does not depend on the leader switch. /pokegyms config leader only stops new registrations; challenges keep working.

docs.title: Leader dialogue
docs.text:
The leader NPC of a player-held gym talks at five moments of a challenge, in Cobblemon's own dialogue box with the NPC's name and face.

Moment When Default line Before the battle The challenger right-clicks the leader. The box shows first and the battle starts when it is closed. "So you have come to challenge this gym. Show me what you have got!" Last Pokémon left The leader is down to its last Pokémon. It is a line in the battle log. "My last Pokémon... I am not done yet!" You win The leader wins. Shown about 2 seconds after the battle ends. "Not this time. Train harder and come back." You lose The leader loses. Shown about 2 seconds after the battle ends. "Well fought. You have earned it." Challenger back too soon A challenger tries again before their rematch cooldown is over. Also a line in chat. "Back already? Rest your team and come back later."

"You win" and "You lose" are from the NPC's side: the first is what the leader says after beating the challenger.

  • The holder writes the lines. On the Team tab, the leader clicks Dialogue (bottom left) and types a line for each moment. An empty line uses the default, shown greyed in the field. All five are saved together.
  • Lines belong to the licence. A new leader, or one who takes the gym over, starts on the defaults, and when a licence ends the lines go with it.
  • Limits. A line is at most dialogue.max_length characters (120 by default, up to 256). A longer line, or one with a formatting code (§) or a control character, is refused and nothing is saved.
  • Disciples say the same moments with the default lines.
  • Only player gyms. City leaders and RCT trainers keep their own dialogue.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config dialogue enabled false: nobody speaks and the battle starts at once. The saved lines are kept for when it is back on.

docs.title: Where the battle happens
docs.text:
A leader battle is staged at the gym, in singles and in doubles. It applies to the City leader and to the leader of a player-held gym, not to disciple battles, which are not moved.

  • You are moved. When the battle starts you are taken to the gym's challenger spot, facing the leader.
  • Each side's Pokémon have a spot. Yours come out at the challenger's Pokémon spot and the leader's at its own, and they come back there after a switch.
  • Doubles spread out. Two Pokémon of one side stand side by side, across the line toward the other side, staging.doubles_gap blocks apart (3 by default, 1 to 8).
  • A gym without those spots battles as before. Gyms the server recorded before 0.0.43 have none, so Cobblemon places everything as it always did. A gym with only some of the spots uses those it has.
  • Other mods' battle blocks never take it over. Only PokeGyms' own leader battles are placed, matched by the battle itself, so a battle block of another mod nearby (such as Cobblemon Battle Positions) leaves a gym battle alone, and every other battle is left alone too.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config staging enabled false: nobody is moved and Cobblemon places everything.
  • Not in real-time fights. A fight Cobblemon Action Combat runs in real time is not staged.

docs.title: With Cobblemon Action Combat
docs.text:
Cobblemon Action Combat is optional, on Fabric and on NeoForge. Without it nothing here applies.

  • Real-time gym fights count. When its NPC fights are real time, beating a player leader, a disciple or a City leader gives what a turn-based win gives: the medal, the vault share, the City badge and the licence unlock. A loss, a forfeit or running away costs the penalty.
  • The trainer takes the next challenger once the fight is over.
  • PokeGyms has no switch for it. Whether gym fights are real time follows Cobblemon Action Combat's own /cac format.
  • Two things are turn-based only. In real time there is no battle staging and no last-Pokémon line from the leader (see Leader dialogue); the challenge and after-battle lines still show.
  • Operators can check it in the log: Cobblemon Action Combat found: real-time gym fights count like turn-based ones.

docs.title: Rematch cooldown
docs.text:
After you finish a challenge of a player leader, the same leader will not take you on again right away.

  • It starts when the challenge ends, won or lost. Forfeiting or running away counts as a loss. A battle the server stops, with no winner, starts no wait.
  • It is yours alone, and per gym. Another challenger can fight the same leader at once, and you can still fight other gyms' leaders.
  • Trying early is refused, and the message tells you the time left, such as "will take your challenge again in 45 min". The time is rounded up to whole minutes.
  • It lasts 60 minutes by default, and survives a server restart. A gym whose licence ends and is bought again starts with nobody waiting.
  • City leaders have no cooldown. It applies only to player leaders, not to the City (RCT) leaders; the Champion is the one RCT trainer that uses it.
  • Operators can change it with /pokegyms config rematch: cooldown_minutes sets the wait (0 means no wait), and enabled switches the whole cooldown off.

docs.title: Taking over a gym
docs.text:
Beat a player leader, keep the medal they gave you, and you can take their gym.

  • Where. Open the gym's Gym Manager and go to the Licence tab, which a visitor and a disciple of the gym both see. It shows the Fee, what you have and a Take over button. A holder cannot take their own gym.
  • What you need. The medal, in your main hand, and the takeover fee, 10,000 CobbleDollars by default. The fee is destroyed, never paid to anyone, and the medal is used up. A Badge It badge works too, if it is the signed copy you won.
  • Only the real medal. It must name this gym and its current leader. The server refuses an empty hand, a badge crafted by hand (it has no PokeGyms signature), a medal of another gym, a medal of an earlier leader of this gym, your own gym, a leader in the middle of a battle, too little money, and a server with takeovers switched off. You are told why in chat.
  • It works on any gym a player holds, a town gym or a City gym.
  • No shield. The new leader gets the whole vault and keeps the gym's disciples (if they were one of them, they are no longer one). The old leader loses the licence, and the gym's team, penalty, registered Badge It medal and rematch waits go with it: register your own team in the Team tab. The old leader is told in chat if they are online.
  • Your own gym goes first. One licence per player: if you already held a gym, you give it up before the takeover and it goes vacant (or, in a City gym, back to its leader), its vault paid to you.
  • Operators can switch it off or change the fee with /pokegyms config takeover.

docs.title: Medals
docs.text:
Beating a player leader gives you a Gym Medal.

  • One medal, for every gym. It is a single generic item, a gold-rimmed Poké Ball on a red and white ribbon, with no art of its own per gym. It does not show in the creative tab; a medal only comes from a win.
  • It is signed. Hover it to read the gym ("Pewter City Gym" for a City gym, otherwise "Gym at" its coordinates), "Leader:" with the name of the player you beat, and "Won on" with the date of the win.
  • Only a win gives one. A loss, a forfeit, or a battle the server stops gives none, and so does a win against a City (RCT) leader: medals are for player leaders. The leader gets none either.
  • You get one per win. Winning the same gym again, after the rematch cooldown, gives another.
  • A full inventory is no loss. The medal drops at your feet.
  • With Badge It, the medal can be a badge. Badge It is optional. When it is installed, the holder's Team tab has a third row, Medal: hold one of its badges in your main hand and click it to register that badge as the gym's medal (you keep the badge). Winners then get a copy of that badge signed the same way, with the gym, the leader and the date in its lore. A badge crafted by hand carries no signature. Without Badge It, or before a badge is registered, winners get the generic medal. A gym's new licence starts without a badge.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config medals enabled false: no win gives a medal, and medals already given stay.

docs.title: Mainline badges
docs.text:
With PKGBadges installed, beating a City leader gives you the badge that leader gives in the main games: Brock the Boulder Badge, Misty the Cascade Badge, and so on. PKGBadges is optional.

  • The 16 Kanto and Johto leaders have one. Radical Cobblemon Trainers' leaders from the main games (Brock to Giovanni, Falkner to Clair) give their badge; the other City leaders give none.
  • Once per challenger. Winning again gives nothing more, and it stays so after the gym's licence ends and the City leader is back.
  • A full inventory is no loss. The badge drops at your feet.
  • Only a win against a City leader gives one. A loss, a forfeit, a stopped battle, and a win against a player leader give none (those give a medal).
  • Datapacks can change the map. data/cobblemon_pokegyms/badges.json maps a leader to an item id. A key is an RCT trainer id, or a leader's name, which covers all that leader's variants; a leader with no entry gives nothing (the server logs it once). Without PKGBadges no badge is given, and the start-up log says so.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config badges enabled false: no win gives a badge, and badges already given stay.

docs.title: Level scaling
docs.text:
A gym leader's team fights at your level, whatever levels it was registered at. So does the team of every other Radical Cobblemon Trainers (RCT) trainer, including the ones wandering the world.

  • The level is your best Pokémon's. It is the highest level in your whole party, fainted Pokémon included, so a Pokémon you cannot send out still counts. The team scales up and down alike: a level 20 team meets a level 50 challenger at 50, and a level 80 team meets a level 30 one at 30.
  • Every Pokémon of the team is set to it, at full HP. It is capped at the server's maximum Pokémon level.
  • It covers every RCT trainer, in a gym or out of it. The City leaders and the trainers you meet in the world are RCT trainers, and so every battle against one is scaled. The player leaders are scaled too.
  • Each Pokémon takes the evolution stage of its new level. A registered Charizard faced at level 12 is a Charmander, and a Charmander faced at level 40 is a Charizard. It goes up and down alike, and only level evolutions are crossed, so a Vaporeon stays a Vaporeon. A Pokémon holding an Everstone keeps its species both ways. Where an evolution branches, the first one that applies is taken.
  • Empty move slots are filled for the new level. The moves a Pokémon was registered with stay in their slots, even one its new stage cannot learn. Each empty slot gets the newest level-up move its stage knows at the new level that it does not already have. A Pokémon registered with four moves fights with exactly those four.
  • Only the battle changes. The Team tab, a holder's registered team and RCT's trainer data keep their levels; the scaled Pokémon are copies made for that battle alone, so a trainer's team is the same when you meet it again at another level.
  • A format with its own fixed level keeps it. If the battle format sets a level for everyone, the opponent's team is not scaled.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config scaling enabled false: teams then fight at their registered levels, RCT trainers' included. Battles already running keep the levels they started with. /pokegyms config evolution enabled false keeps only the evolution stages out: levels still scale, species stay as registered.

docs.title: Battle rules
docs.text:
The server can ban Terastallization, Dynamax, Mega Evolution, Z-Moves and held items in gym battles, and a leader can ban more for their own gym. All five are allowed by default.

  • Who is held to them. Only the gym's side: a player leader, their disciples, a City leader, its disciples and the Champion. The challenger battles as always, with every gimmick and item they have. A City gym and the Champion follow the server's rules alone; they have no leader to add any.
  • The server's rules. The rules group of the config has one switch per ban: allow_tera, allow_dynamax, allow_mega, allow_z and allow_held_items. In the file they are true or false; with /pokegyms config rules <setting> a 0 bans and a 1 allows. rules.enabled false turns every ban off, the leaders' too, and they count again when it is back on. A battle keeps the rules it started under.
  • The leader's rules. In the Gym Manager's Team tab the Rules row shows how many bans the gym's battles run under, the server's included, or All allowed. Click it for a screen with one button per rule, switching it between Allowed and Banned; Done saves all five and Cancel goes back. A leader can only tighten: what the server bans shows Banned by the server, greyed out, and cannot be switched. The row sits after Format and Team (and after the Badge It medal row when Badge It is installed), and is not there while rules is off. A new licence or a takeover starts with none of its own.
  • Items. A banned held item is taken off the gym's Pokémon in the battle only. The registered team and RCT's trainers keep theirs afterwards.
  • Gimmicks. A banned gimmick is never offered to the gym's side, whatever runs its turns, so the Pokémon keeps its Tera type and its stone and still cannot use them. Banning Z-Moves bans Ultra Burst too.

docs.title: The Gym Manager
docs.text:
Every gym has a Gym Manager: a lectern just inside the gym's door. It is put there as soon as the gym is found and the spot is loaded.

  • It cannot be broken in survival and drops nothing. A Gym Manager removed in creative comes back the next time its chunk loads.
  • It comes in three looks, wood, tech and Poké Ball. They behave the same; a City gym's is the Poké Ball one. All three are in the PokeGyms creative tab, for builders.
  • A Gym Manager placed by hand somewhere that is not a gym's spot belongs to no gym, and says so when right-clicked.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
Right-clicking a Gym Manager opens its screen, built on Cobblemon's summary screen:

  • The header names the gym by its city, such as Pewter City Gym, with a CITY tag, and who runs it: the City leader.
  • The Info tab, which everyone sees, gives the gym's kind (City gym), its status (Canonical) and its location (X, Z), and in a City gym the type of its leader, with a short line about who runs it. At a City gym whose leader you beat, the line says you may buy its licence.
  • The Team tab, which only the holder sees, registers the gym's team and has the Dialogue button for the leader's lines and a Rules row for the battle rules.
  • The Licence tab is where a visitor or a disciple of a held gym can take it over.
  • The Disciples tab is seen by the holder, by a player the holder invited and by the gym's disciples: see Disciples.
  • The Roster tab is seen by a visitor and by a player the holder invited, not by the holder or the gym's disciples: see Challenging a gym.
  • The gym team panel on the side has six slots. They show the registered team by name and level, and stand empty while the gym has none.

The screen shows the gym as the server saw it when you opened it, and every button asks the server again before anything happens.

The holder's screen has four tabs: Info, Licence, Team and Disciples. A disciple sees Info, Licence and Disciples. A visitor sees Info, Licence (when there is a licence to buy or a gym to take over) and Roster. The Licence tab also holds the gym's vault: its penalty, Withdraw and Renounce. See Licences.

docs.title: Disciples
docs.text:
A player leader can have up to three disciples: other players who train under them and stand in the gym as trainers.

  • Invite from the Disciples tab. The holder opens the Disciples tab of the Gym Manager, clicks the Invite row to pick one of the players online who is not yet anyone's disciple, and presses Invite. The player is told in chat.
  • The invited player accepts at that gym's Gym Manager, with the Accept button of the same tab, and takes the first free disciple_N place of the gym. A fourth invitation is refused: the gym has three places.
  • A disciple registers a team, like the leader: press Register (or Update) and the gym keeps a frozen copy of the party they carry, in the gym's format, singles while the leader has not registered a team. Singles needs 1 Pokémon in the party, doubles 2. Their own Pokémon stay with them.
  • A trainer NPC stands for it. Gym Trainer <player>, wearing the disciple's skin and carrying the copy, stands at their place.
  • One gym at a time. A player is the disciple of a single gym on the server. It needs no licence, so a disciple may hold one at another gym.
  • The leader removes a disciple with a shift-click on their row in the holder's Disciples tab; the NPC goes. When the leader's licence ends, every disciple goes with it.
  • The leader can share the vault with them. Each disciple's row shows their share of the gym's vault (Name 25%), a click on it gives them 5% more, and a Leader row shows what the leader keeps. A withdrawal, or the end of the licence, pays everyone their share.
  • Colours in the holder's list: a disciple's name is white once they registered a team, gold until then, and a free place reads grey.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config disciples enabled false: nobody can be invited or register, and disciples already there stay until the leader removes them.

docs.title: Challenging the disciples
docs.text:
Right-clicking a disciple's trainer NPC challenges it, like the leader: a fresh copy of its team at your level, in the gym's current format.

  • Fight them in order. The disciples that have registered a team are fought in order, disciple 1, 2, 3, and the leader takes your challenge only once you have beaten every one. A gym with no disciples is challenged at the leader directly.
  • Progress is kept when you log out or the server restarts, until you lose.
  • A loss to any disciple costs you the gym's penalty, starts the rematch cooldown and sends you back to disciple 1.
  • Beating a disciple pays nothing: no winner's share, no medal and no cooldown. A finished leader challenge, won or lost, starts the next one from disciple 1.
  • Changes start everyone over. A disciple joining, registering again or leaving, or a new licence, resets every challenger's progress.
  • Who cannot challenge. The holder and the gym's own disciples. Each trainer battles one challenger at a time.

docs.title: Challenging a gym
docs.text:
A visitor's Gym Manager has a Roster tab, titled Order, that lists the gym's trainers in the order you face them: its disciples one after another, the leader last.

  • Beaten trainers are struck out, the one you face next is gold and the rest wait.
  • Press Challenge and the next trainer takes you on at their place, the same as right-clicking them. The screen closes for the battle.
  • Only the next trainer can be called out. A disciple you beat cannot be fought again until you start over, after a loss or a finished challenge against the leader. If you try anyway, or the gym takes no challenge from you now, you are told in chat.
  • A trainer who is not at their place yet asks you to try again in a moment.
  • City gyms work the same way, with their RCT disciples first and the City leader last.
  • A player the holder invited sees the tab too, while they decide on the invitation.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config roster enabled false: challengers get no Roster tab; right-clicking a trainer still challenges it, in the same order.

docs.title: Gym battles
docs.text:
A battle against an NPC trainer who stands inside a gym, such as a Cities & Structures gym leader, is a gym battle from its start until it ends. PokeGyms marks it, so other mods can tell it apart, and the gym's side fights under the battle rules. Mid-Battle EXP uses this to give more EXP in gyms.

Each gym battle knows its gym and who the challenger faces: the gym's leader, a disciple, or the City gym's canonical leader. Operators can list the gym battles running now with /pokegyms battles.

docs.title: For mod authors
docs.text:
Ask through com.shier.pokegyms.api.GymBattleApi. Every method is a JVM static, so a mod that does not depend on PokeGyms can call it by reflection:

Method Returns isGymBattle(battleId: UUID) Whether the Cobblemon battle is a gym battle. opponent(battleId: UUID) leader, disciple or canonical_leader; null when it is not a gym battle. marker(battleId: UUID) The whole marker (dimension, gym origin, opponent), for a mod compiled against PokeGyms; null when it is not a gym battle. 
val gym = runCatching {
    Class.forName("com.shier.pokegyms.api.GymBattleApi")
        .getMethod("isGymBattle", UUID::class.java)
        .invoke(null, battle.battleId) as Boolean
}.getOrDefault(false) // PokeGyms not installed

docs.title: Licences
docs.text:
A licence is what lets a player run a gym as its leader. The rules below are in the mod today.

A City gym's licence has to be earned

Every gym in this build is a City gym, led by an RCT leader. Its licence is for sale only to a player who beat that leader; to everyone else the Licence tab does not appear.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
• One licence per player on the whole server, whatever the dimension.
  • It costs 25,000 CobbleDollars by default, paid at the gym's Gym Manager. The server sets the price (Configuration).
  • A City gym sells its licence only to a player who beat its leader, at the same price and with the same one licence per player. Beating them is remembered even with licences switched off. While the gym is held its leader is gone; when the licence ends the leader is back and the gym is locked again for everyone, the former holder included.
  • A held gym can be taken over with its leader's medal and a fee, which moves the licence to the taker; see Taking over a gym. The taker's own previous licence is given up first.
  • It ends after 30 days without logging in by default, or when its holder renounces it. Either way a town gym goes vacant, anyone can buy it again, and the former holder may buy another (a City gym goes back to its leader, as above). The server checks when it starts and once a day after. With the days set to 0, a licence never expires.

docs.title: The Licence tab
docs.text:
At a vacant town gym, a City gym whose leader you beat, or a gym a player holds, the Gym Manager screen adds a Licence tab:

  • For a visitor: the price, how many CobbleDollars you have, and a Buy button. If you already hold a licence, the tab says which gym it is; if you are short, it says how much more you need. The server checks the price and your balance again when you click.
  • At a gym a player holds (a visitor, or a disciple of that gym): the takeover fee, how many CobbleDollars you have and a Take over button. Hold the leader's medal in your main hand when you click; see Taking over a gym.
  • For the holder: the gym's vault and its Penalty (click the row to raise it, shift-click to lower it), when the licence expires (Expiry), the penalty's Range (only while penalties are on), a Withdraw button in the bottom-left box and a Renounce button in the bottom-right one, which asks for a second click to confirm and pays the vault out, split with the disciples if you set shares.

docs.title: After a crash
docs.text:
When the server starts, it checks every licence against the gym it names, and the gym wins: a licence whose gym no longer names its player is dropped, a gym naming a holder the licence list forgot is added to it, and if one player ends up holding two gyms, the second goes vacant. Each fix is written to the server log. Licences of gyms in a dimension that is not loaded are left alone.

Switching licences off (Configuration) stops every gym from selling its licence. Licences already held stay, and still expire or can be renounced.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: There is no Gym Manager in a city
docs.text:
• The city has no gym building: Lavender and Pallet never have one, and the other cities do not always build theirs. /pokegyms gyms lists the gyms the server found in your dimension.
  • Cobblemon Cities & Structures is not installed on the server. Without it PokeGyms finds no gyms.
  • The spot has not loaded yet. The Gym Manager is placed when its chunk is loaded; walk into the gym.

docs.title: /pokegyms gyms says "No gyms recorded"
docs.text: No Cities & Structures city with a gym has loaded in that dimension yet, or Cities & Structures is missing. Gyms are found as their cities load, so explore first.

docs.title: The game will not start and names a mod
docs.text: One of the requirements is missing or older than PokeGyms needs. The message says which and which version; install that one.

docs.title: Right-clicking a Gym Manager says it belongs to no gym
docs.text: That lectern was placed by hand, not by PokeGyms. Only the Gym Manager standing at a gym's own spot opens the gym's screen.

docs.title: There is no Licence tab
docs.text: That is expected in this build: no gym sells a licence yet (Licences).

docs.title: The config file did not take my change
docs.text: It is read when the server starts. On a live server, use /pokegyms config instead (Commands & Configuration). If the file is not valid JSON, the server runs on the defaults and says so in its log.

docs.title: The Gym Vault
docs.text:
A player-held gym has a vault: the CobbleDollars that challengers lost to its leader. The holder sets the penalty a challenger risks, and takes the vault's money when they like.

Everything here is on the Licence tab of the Gym Manager, which only the gym's holder sees (see Licences). City gyms led by an RCT leader have no vault; their penalty is destroyed.

docs.title: Setting the penalty
docs.text:
The holder's Licence tab shows the Penalty, what the Vault holds, when the licence expires (Expiry) and the penalty's Range (only while penalties are on).

  • Click the Penalty row to raise it by a tenth of the server's range. Shift-click lowers it. Past either end it wraps round to the other.
  • It stays within the server's range, vault.penalty_min to vault.penalty_max (100 to 10,000 CobbleDollars by default; see Configuration). The server checks it again, so no other amount gets through.
  • A new holder starts on the least.
  • It is locked while your leader is battling. You are told to change it when the battle ends, so a challenger never pays more than they agreed to.

docs.title: Challengers
docs.text:
• You need the penalty in hand to challenge the leader. There are no debts: if you carry less, you are told what it costs and what you have, and the fight does not start.
  • Losing pays it. A loss, a forfeit or running away moves exactly the penalty from you into the vault. You are told what you paid.
  • Winning costs nothing, and neither does a battle the server stops with no winner. A win over a player leader also pays you a share of the vault: see Winner's share.
  • If the gym's licence ends during the battle, or you spent the money meanwhile, nothing moves.

docs.title: Winner's share
docs.text:
Beating a player leader pays you a share of the gym's vault: winner_share.percent of what it holds, 10% by default, rounded down. A vault of 1,000 pays 100 and keeps 900. The chat tells you how much you took.

  • Only the leader pays. Nothing is taken from the vault if the leader is not the one you beat.
  • A vault too small to give a whole CobbleDollar pays nothing.
  • It is paid at once, and if CobbleDollars refuses it, you get it on your next login. The money leaves the vault either way, so it is never lost.
  • Nothing moves if the gym is no longer held, for instance when its licence ended during the battle (the vault has already gone to the holder).
  • Operators can change it with /pokegyms config winner_share: percent from 0 to 100, or enabled false. 0 percent pays nothing too.

docs.title: Splitting the vault
docs.text:
The holder can give each disciple a share of the vault. Open the Disciples tab: each disciple's row shows their name and share (Name 25%), and a last Leader row shows what you keep.

  • Click a disciple to give them 5% more. Once you have nothing left to give, the next click puts them back on 0%. Shift-click still removes the disciple.
  • The shares always add up to 100%. The leader keeps whatever the disciples' shares leave, and the server refuses a split over 100%. Only the holder can set shares.
  • A new disciple starts on 0%. A disciple you remove gives their share back to the leader. After a takeover the new leader keeps the disciples' shares as they were.
  • Changing a share does not restart the challengers' progress through the gym's disciples.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config vault_split enabled false: the whole vault goes to the leader and no share can be set. The shares already set are kept for when it is back on.

docs.title: Withdrawing
docs.text:
Withdraw sits in the bottom-left box of the Licence tab. It appears when the vault holds money and pays all of it out at once: each disciple gets their share, rounded down, and you get the rest, rounding included. With no shares set, all of it goes to you. The vault goes back to 0, and you are told what you kept.

  • A disciple who is online is paid at once and told so.
  • A disciple who is offline is paid on their next login.
  • If CobbleDollars refuses a payment, that player gets it on their next login instead: no one's share is lost.

docs.title: When the licence ends
docs.text: Renouncing (the Renounce button, bottom-right, whose confirm text says you get the vault) or expiring pays the whole vault out before the gym goes vacant, split like a withdrawal: each disciple their share and the holder the rest. The same goes for a gym given up to make a takeover. The gym taken over keeps its vault for the new leader. Anyone who is offline gets their money on their next login, and is told then. The money is not lost if CobbleDollars refuses it: it is kept for the next login.

docs.title: Switching it off
docs.text: With vault.enabled off, no player leader charges a penalty and a challenger needs none to start. The Licence tab says penalties are off; vaults keep what they hold, can still be withdrawn, and are still paid out when a licence ends. The winner's share has its own switch and is not turned off by it.
